title: k8s-node-lifecycle-debug-breadcrumbs-2
content:
Notes / breadcrumbs for the node lifecycle provisioning flapping incident (dev cluster).

Summary: New nodes intermittently go NotReady shortly after provisioning (within 5-15 minutes). Symptoms vary: kubelet crashes, CNI failing to configure, or heavy disk IO causing slow boot. Hypothesis: cloud-init + kubelet startup race + CNI plugin (flannel) incompatible config / MTU mismatch. Also seen on a subset of instance types (g5-small).

Commands tried (chronological):
- aws ec2 describe-instances --filters "Name=tag:Name,Values=k8s-worker-*" --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].[InstanceId,State.Name,InstanceType,PrivateIpAddress,Tags]'
- ssh ubuntu@ip
- sudo systemctl status kubelet
- sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager
- sudo journalctl -k -b --no-pager | tail -n 80
- sudo docker ps -a || sudo crictl ps -a
- kubectl get nodes -o wide
- kubectl describe node <node-name>
- kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide | egrep 'calico|kube-proxy|kubelet|flannel'
- ip a; ip route; cat /etc/cni/net.d/*; lsmod | egrep 'vxlan|ip_vs'
- helm list -n kube-system; helm upgrade --install flannel ./charts/flannel -f values-flannel.yaml --namespace kube-system
- sudo kubeadm token list
- sudo kubeadm join <control-plane-ip>:6443 --token <token> --discovery-token-ca-cert-hash sha256:<hash>
- sudo cat /var/log/cloud-init-output.log
- dmesg | tail -n 50

Relevant error snippets (copied from journalctl / kubelet logs):
- "level=error msg=\"Failed to create pod infra container\" error=\"failed to setup network for pod...: CNI network configuration not found for network 'pod-net'\""
- "Jan 22 12:03:14 node kubelet[1234]: E0222 12:03:14.456789    1234 kubelet.go:2190] node not ready: Kubelet has no node IP address"
- "Feb 10 09:14:02 kubelet[2345]: error: failed to run Kubelet: failed to create Kubelet: context deadline exceeded"
- "Feb 10 09:14:05 cloud-init[123]: Running apt-get update... failed: Could not fetch http://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/dists/...  temporary failure resolving 'archive.ubuntu.com'"
- "flannel.1: Waiting for network config" / "W0310 00:00:01.000000 1 main.go:123] Could not read CNI config: open /etc/cni/net.d/10-flannel.conflist: no such file or directory"
- "kube-proxy crashloopbackoff: failed to write iptables rules: permission denied (operation not permitted)"

Observed patterns: 
- Nodes that show DNS resolution issues in cloud-init tend to fail to pull container images and then kubelet times out.
- Some nodes hit a transient API server auth error during bootstrap: "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority"; seems related to token exchange timing.
- MTU mismatch suspected: pods on problematic nodes show excessive retransmits; flannel config uses vxlan with mtu 1450 but host eni has 9001 (jumbo) on certain instance types -> fragmentation.
- disk pressure not common, but one node had slow /var/lib/kubelet OOMs and kubelet restarted repeatedly.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) race between cloud-init installing CNI files and kubelet starting -> kubelet starts and sees missing CNI config -> pods fail -> kubelet restarts later but cluster marks NotReady during window. Fix: delay kubelet start until CNI installed or make cloud-init write CNI first.
2) CNI incompat with MTU on g5-small instances causing flannel vxlan fragmentation and heavy packet loss -> flannel stalls. Fix: set flannel.mtu = 9001 for those instance types or set host MTU to 1450.
3) transient DNS outbound failures in cloud-init (resolver config) cause image pulls to fail -> kubelet timeouts. Fix: add retry logic to cloud-init or ensure DHCP/resolv.conf present before package install.
4) CRI mismatch (containerd vs docker) - some images rely on docker-shim paths. Fix: standardize to containerd + patch images.

Temporary mitigations tried: 
- Tainted new nodes with NoSchedule until post-bootstrap health-check passed. kubectl taint nodes <node> node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable=true:NoSchedule (worked to protect workloads).
- Pulled flannel manifest manually and applied as DaemonSet earlier in bootstrap before kubelet start. Reduced failures in ~60% of cases.
- Added systemd drop-in to kubelet.service to add "ExecStartPre=/bin/sleep 10" (kludge) to give cloud-init a bit more time. Mixed results.

Next steps / TODO (concrete):
- [ ] Add preflight check in cloud-init: wait for resolvability (curl -sI https://google.com) and for /etc/cni/net.d to exist and contain 10-flannel.conflist before finishing provisioning. Log timings.
- [ ] Adjust flannel Helm values to set mtu per instance-type via templating. Add a cluster-autoscaler hook to set correct values.
- [ ] Instrument node bootstrap logs upload to S3 for flaky nodes (cloud-init to scp/jq logs).
- [ ] Create a small canary pool (3 nodes) with modified cloud-init and flannel MTU and run for 48 hours.
- [ ] Add kubelet systemd unit ordering: ensure cni config unit runs before kubelet (systemd unit to wait on /etc/cni/net.d).
- [ ] Reproduce on a g5-small locally by forcing MTU mismatch and confirm flannel behavior.

Notes to self / quick commands to rerun when debugging next occurrence: 
- kubectl describe node <node> | egrep -A5 'Conditions|Taints|Addresses'
- sudo journalctl -u cloud-init -n 400 --no-pager | sed -n '1,200p'
- sudo journalctl -u kubelet -b --no-pager | sed -n '1,300p'
- curl -vvv --resolve archive.ubuntu.com:80:1.2.3.4 http://archive.ubuntu.com
- sudo ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1450; systemctl restart flanneld; journalctl -u flanneld -f

Past patches / references: 
- infra PR #342: add start delay for kubelet on cloud-init (temporary, reverted)
- Confluence doc: k8s-node-provisioning-runbook (linked above)

If this spikes again, escalate to SRE oncall (pager: @sre-oncall) and attach following logs: cloud-init-output.log, journalctl kubelet last 500 lines, /var/log/cloud-init.log, /etc/cni/net.d contents, ip route output, ifconfig/ip a.

End of breadcrumbs.

-- Jordan
